Miller''' (born February 19, 1980) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player and coach. He played 17 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) after being selected by the [[Orlando Magic]] in the first round of the [[2000 NBA draft]] with the fifth overall pick. Miller was named the [[NBA Rookie of the Year]] with the Magic in 2001 and was voted [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year]] with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in 2006. He won two consecutive [[NBA championship]]s with the [[Miami Heat]] in 2012 and 2013. Miller played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]] before entering the NBA. He also played professionally for the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], [[Washington Wizards]], [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], and [[Denver Nuggets]]. He was a [[swingman]] who was primarily a three-point specialist.{{cite web|last=Brewer |first=Jerry |url=http://articles.orlandosentinel.com/keyword/mike-miller |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100924194201/http://articles.orlandosentinel.com/keyword/mike-miller |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 24, 2010 |title=Articles about Mike Miller |publisher= Orlando Sentinel |date=August 28, 2012 |access-date=July 17, 2013}} After his playing career, he became a college assistant coach with the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]]. He resigned after two seasons before becoming the head coach at Houston High. He coached Houston High to their first ever basketball state championship winning 62–43 on March 20, 2021 in his only season with the school. In 2020, Miller founded Let It Fly Team Sports Management, a full-service agency that represents college and professional football and basketball players. His clients include Orlando Magic forward Paolo Banchero and New Orleans Pelicans point guard Jeremiah Fears.{{Cite web |last=Martin |first=John |title=Now an agent, Mike Miller is poised to make noise at NBA draft |url=https://dailymemphian.com/article/29145/memphis-tigers-coach-mike-miller-lift-agent-nba-draft |access-date=2026-02-28 |website=Memphis Local, Sports, Business & Food News {{!}} Daily Memphian |language=en}} ==College career== Miller accepted an athletic scholarship to attend the [[University of Florida]], where he played for coach [[Billy Donovan]]'s [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Gators]] teams from 1998 until 2000. He quickly became known for his ability to hit the [[three-point field goal|three-pointer]]. As a sophomore, Miller helped the Gators avoid an upset bid by Butler in the first round of the [[2000 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Tournament]], winning 69–68 in overtime on his floater in the lane as the buzzer sounded. This fueled the Gators' path to the 2000 NCAA Championship game, ultimately losing to [[1999–2000 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]]. After the 2000 NCAA Tournament, Miller declared himself eligible for the NBA draft.{{cite news | last=Korth | first=Joanne | title=Miller says he will enter NBA draft | date=April 21, 2000 | url=https://www.tampabay.com/archive/2000/04/21/miller-says-he-will-enter-nba-draft/ | work=Tampa Bay Times }} ==Professional career== ===Orlando Magic (2000–2003)=== The following summer, Miller was taken with the fifth overall pick in the [[2000 NBA draft]] by the [[Orlando Magic]]. His debut game was played on October 31, 2000, in a 97–86 win over the [[Washington Wizards]] where he recorded 5 points, 2 rebounds and 3 steals.{{cite web | url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/200010310ORL.html | title=Wizards vs Magic, October 31, 2000 }} Miller won the 2001 [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award]] while being the only first-year player to appear in all 82 regular season games during the [[2000–01 NBA season|2000–01 season]] (starting 62), in which he averaged 11.9 points and 4.0 rebounds per game while shooting 40.7% from [[Three-point field goal|three-point range]]. ===Memphis Grizzlies (2003–2008)=== Miller was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] alongside [[Ryan Humphrey]] midway through [[2002–03 NBA season]] for [[Gordan Giriček]] and [[Drew Gooden (basketball)|Drew Gooden]]. On October 4, 2003, Miller signed a six-year, $47.25 million extension through the 2009–10 season. He was the recipient of the [[NBA Sixth Man of the Year Award]] for the [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]]. He averaged 13.7 points 5.4 rebounds 2.7 assists while shooting 47% from the field and 41% from [[Three-point field goal|three]], while playing 30.6 minutes per game. On January 3, 2007, Miller made nine three-pointers in a win over the [[Golden State Warriors]], breaking [[Sam Mack]]'s Grizzlies franchise record of eight in a game set in February 1999.[http://www.commercialappeal.com/mca/grizzlies/article/0,1426,MCA_475_5255438,00.html Grizzlies reach 144 in the 'old ball' game : Grizzlies : Commercial Appeal] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930155311/http://www.commercialappeal.com/mca/grizzlies/article/0,1426,MCA_475_5255438,00.html |date=September 30, 2007 }} The two previous games Miller hit seven threes.[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270103029 Miller's season-high 33 leads way for Grizzlies] January 03, 2007 This made him the first NBA player to hit at least seven three-pointers in three consecutive games[https://www.espn.com/espn/news/story?id=2719469 Elias Says ... Arenas gone wild] ESPN since the [[Dallas Mavericks]]' [[George McCloud]] achieved it in 1996.[http://www.basketballreference.com/players/playerlog.htm?yr=1995&ilkid=MCCLOGE01 databaseBasketball.com] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071023073520/http://www.basketballreference.com/players/playerlog.htm?yr=1995&ilkid=MCCLOGE01 |date=October 23, 2007 }} Miller held the Memphis Grizzlies franchise record for most points scored in a single game, with 45 on February 21, 2007, against the [[Golden State Warriors]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270221009 Miller scores franchise-record 45 pts. in Grizzlies loss] The record was later broken by [[Ja Morant]] in February 2022.{{Cite web |title=Ja Morant sets Memphis Grizzlies mark with 46 points to beat Chicago Bulls |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33381807/ja-morant-sets-memphis-grizzlies-mark-46-points-beat-chicago-bulls |access-date=February 27, 2022 |website=ESPN|date=February 27, 2022 }} After the 2006–07 NBA season, Miller was announced as a member of the USA Basketball team. ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2008–2009)=== On June 26, 2008, Miller, [[Brian Cardinal]], [[Jason Collins]], and the 5th pick of the [[2008 NBA draft]], [[Kevin Love]], were sent to Minnesota in exchange for [[Marko Jarić]], [[Antoine Walker]], [[Greg Buckner]] and the 3rd pick, [[O. J. Mayo]].Chad Ford [https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2008/news/story?id=3463045 Mayo heads to Memphis, Love to Minnesota in blockbuster trade] Miller averaged a career-high 4.5 assists per game but a career-low 9.9 points per game in his only season with the Timberwolves. ===Washington Wizards (2009–2010)=== [[File:Mike Miller.jpg|thumb|Miller with the Wizards in 2009]] On June 23, 2009, Miller and [[Randy Foye]] were sent to the [[Washington Wizards]] for [[Oleksiy Pecherov]], [[Etan Thomas]], [[Darius Songaila]] and the 5th overall pick in the [[2009 NBA draft]].{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4282279 |title=Source: Deal sends Minnesota Timberwolves' Randy Foye, Mike Miller to Washington Wizards |work=ESPN |date=June 24, 2009 |access-date=December 18, 2010}} Miller suffered a shoulder injury and missed a few games during the early part of the 2009–10 NBA season.{{cite news | title=Wizards' Miller sprains shoulder | date=November 4, 2009 | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4624419 | work=espn.com }} In 54 games, he averaged 10.9 points per game, his last-ever double-digit scoring average in a season, but was second in the league in three-point field goal accuracy, at 48.0%.{{Cite web|title=2009-10 NBA Player Stats: Totals (3P%)|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/leagues/NBA_2010_totals.html#totals_stats::fg3|access-date=October 19, 2020|website=basketball-reference.com}} ===Miami Heat (2010–2013)=== On July 15, 2010, Miller signed a five-year, $25 million contract with the [[Miami Heat]], reuniting with his former Gators teammate [[Udonis Haslem]]. He injured his thumb while guarding [[LeBron James]] in practice during the preseason, sidelining him for several weeks.{{cite news |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news;_ylt=Al2iFwDBo_9fCHNBAccT6VW8vLYF?slug=ap-heat-miller |title=Miller injured thumb trying to guard James |agency= Associated Press |date= October 24, 2010 |publisher= Yahoo! Sports |access-date=October 24, 2010}}{{cite web |url=http://www.miamiherald.com/2010/12/18/1979221/miller-close-to-returning.html |title=Miller close to returning |author= Joseph Goodman |date= October 24, 2010 |publisher= Miami Herald |access-date=December 18, 2010}} Miller officially returned to the Miami Heat lineup on December 20, 2010, in a home game against the Dallas Mavericks. Miller got his first start on January 22, 2011, due to a [[Dwyane Wade]] illness, and contributed with a season-high 32 points in a win over the Toronto Raptors. Miller averaged just 2.6 points a game in 12 minutes a game during the playoffs, with a high of 12 in game 4 against the [[Chicago Bulls]]. Miller made his first career NBA Finals appearance in the [[2011 NBA Finals]], which the Heat lost to the Mavericks 4–2. In [[2011–12 Miami Heat season|the next season]], on January 18, 2012, Miller made six of six three-point field goals in a victory over the [[San Antonio Spurs]] to finish with 18 points in his return to the Heat, after missing several games because of an injury.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=320117014|title = Spurs vs. Heat - Game Recap - January 17, 2012 - ESPN}} In the playoffs, Miller averaged 5.2 points per game, and scored in double figures at least once in each of the Heat's playoff series as Miami advanced to the NBA Finals to face the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. In game 5, Miller made seven three-pointers, setting the NBA Finals record for most three-pointers by a reserve."[http://www.gainesville.com/article/20120622/ARTICLES/120629816/-1/news?Title=Heat-G-Miller-says-he-has-tough-decision-to-make- Heat G Miller says he has tough decision to make]". Associated Press. ''Gainesville Sun''. June 22, 2012. Retrieved on June 23, 2012. He had not made any three-pointers in the previous four games of the series. He finished with 23 points,[https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/fl-xpm-2012-06-22-sfl-miami-heat-mike-miller-nba-finals-oklahoma-city-20120621-story.html Heat's Mike Miller shines in potentially his last game] 5 rebounds and a steal in game 5. Miami would go on to win the game and the NBA championship. During the 2012–13 season, Miller was inserted into the starting lineup 17 times and averaged 4.8 points per game for the season. The Heat would again advance to the NBA Finals, this time against the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. Miller was inserted into the last 4 games of the Finals to help space the floor, and scored 8 points in game 6 as the Heat barely squeaked out a victory. One highlight of the game was a three-pointer he made while wearing one shoe. The Heat won the series in game 7 on June 20, 2013, giving Miller his second championship. On July 16, 2013, Miller was waived by the Miami Heat via the [[amnesty clause]].{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news_recap/heat-waive-mike-miller | title=HEAT Waive Mike Miller | work=NBA.com |date=July 16, 2013 | access-date=July 16, 2013}} ===Return to Memphis (2013–2014)=== On July 30, 2013, Miller signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/07/30/grizzlies-sign-miller.ap/ |title=Grizzlies sign, re-introduce 3-point specialist Miller |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=October 10, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171214015009/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/07/30/grizzlies-sign-miller.ap/ |archive-date=December 14, 2017 |url-status=dead }} He saw his minutes and his importance increase with the slightly revamped Grizzlies team led by the new coach [[Dave Joerger]]. Miller played steadily for much of the season, finishing off as the only Grizzly to play all 82 regular season games and all 7 playoff games.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/m/millemi01/gamelog/2014/ Mike Miller 2013-14 Game Log] ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2014–2015)=== On August 5, 2014, Miller signed a two-year, $5.5 million contract with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{cite press release|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/miller-jones-signing-140805 |title=Cavaliers Sign Mike Miller and James Jones |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |date=August 5, 2014 |access-date=August 5, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160627175133/http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/miller-jones-signing-140805 |archive-date=June 27, 2016 }} In Cleveland, he reunited with former [[Miami Heat]] teammates [[LeBron James]] and [[James Jones (basketball, born 1980)|James Jones]], and former [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] teammate [[Kevin Love]]. After averaging just 1.5 points in 12 minutes per game over the first 24 games of the season, Miller made his first start for the Cavaliers on December 19, 2014, against the Brooklyn Nets as he scored 21 points on 7-of-8 three-pointers in the 95–91 win.[http://www.nba.com/games/20141219/BKNCLE/gameinfo.html James, Miller lead Cavaliers over Nets 95-91] The Cavaliers made it to the [[2015 NBA Finals]], but they lost to the [[Golden State Warriors]] in six games. On June 30, 2015, Miller exercised his player option with the Cavaliers for the 2016 season.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/miller-option-150630|title=Mike Miller Exercises 2015-16 Player Option|date=June 30, 2015|work=NBA.com|access-date=June 30, 2015}} On July 27, 2015, Miller was traded, along with [[Brendan Haywood]] and two future second-round draft picks, to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for cash considerations.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Acquire Brendan Haywood, Mike Miller and Draft Picks from Cleveland|url=http://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-acquire-brendan-haywood-mike-miller-and-draft-picks-cleveland|work=NBA.com|date=July 27, 2015|access-date=July 27, 2015}} On September 28, 2015, he was waived by the Trail Blazers via a contract buyout.{{cite web|last=Mutoni|first=Marcel|title=Portland Trail Blazers Buyout Mike Miller|url=http://www.slamonline.com/nba/portland-trail-blazers-buyout-mike-miller/|work=SlamOnline.com|date=September 28, 2015|access-date=September 30, 2015}} ===Denver Nuggets (2015–2017)=== On September 30, 2015, Miller signed with the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/09/30/nuggets-sign-mike-miller.ap/|title=Nuggets sign sharpshooter forward Mike Miller|work=NBA.com|date=September 30, 2015|access-date=September 30, 2015}} Miller was instrumental in the early development of teammate [[Nikola Jokić]].{{cite web|url=https://denverite.com/2016/11/08/denver-nuggets-mike-miller-nikola-jokic-gasol-brothers/|title=Nuggets' Mike Miller: I "see a lot of the Gasol brothers" in Nikola Jokic|work=denverite.com|date=November 8, 2016|access-date=December 14, 2018}} The two players share a special friendship to go along with their mentor/mentee relationship and even share the same birthday.{{cite web|url=https://nugglove.com/2018/11/12/denver-nuggets-holiday-gift-guide/|title=Nikola Jokic and Mike Miller: The Birthday Boys|work=nugglove.com|date=February 19, 2017|access-date=December 14, 2018}} He re-signed with the Nuggets on July 21, 2016 on a two-year, $5 million contract.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-re-sign-mike-miller-072116|title=Denver Nuggets Re-Sign Mike Miller|work=NBA.com|date=July 21, 2016|access-date=July 21, 2016}} Miller's final NBA game was played on April 12, 2017, in a 111–105 victory over the Oklahoma City Thunder where he recorded 8 rebounds and 4 assists, but no points. He was waived by the Denver Nuggets on July 11, 2017.{{cite web|last=Kosminder|first=Nick|url=http://www.denverpost.com/2017/07/11/mike-miller-waived-nuggets/|title=Nuggets waive veteran guard Mike Miller|work=DenverPost.com|date=July 11, 2017|access-date=July 11, 2017}} ==Coaching career== On April 12, 2018, Miller was hired as an assistant coach under [[Penny Hardaway]] at the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|University of Memphis]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/penny-hardaway-hires-nba-champion-mike-miller-for-memphis-staff-larry-brown-next/|title=Penny Hardaway hires NBA champion Mike Miller for Memphis staff; Larry Brown next?|website=cbssports.com|first=Gary|last=Parrish|date=April 5, 2018|access-date=April 7, 2018}}{{cite web |date=April 14, 2018 |title=Memphis hires Mike Miller as Penny Hardaway's assistant coach |url=http://archive.sportando.basketball/en/usa/ncaa/271427/memphis-hires-mike-miller-as-penny-hardaway-s-assistant-coach.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211016000958/http://archive.sportando.basketball/en/usa/ncaa/271427/memphis-hires-mike-miller-as-penny-hardaway-s-assistant-coach.html |archive-date=2021-10-16 |access-date=April 14, 2018 |website=Sportando.basketball}} He spent two seasons with the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Tigers]] and established himself as one of the top [[college recruiting|recruiters]] in the nation. On June 3, 2020, Miller resigned to spend time with his family.{{cite news|last=Borzello|first=Jeff|title=Former NBA player Mike Miller leaving Memphis staff to focus on family|date=June 4, 2020|website=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29262527|access-date=October 19, 2020}} In July, Miller was named the boys basketball coach at [[Houston High School (Germantown, Tennessee)|Houston High School]] in [[Germantown, Tennessee]]. Miller led Houston to the Class AAA State title in his lone season as head coach. His sons Mason and Mavrick were players on the team.{{cite news|first=Khari|last=Thompson|title=Former Memphis assistant Mike Miller hired as Houston boys basketball coach|date=July 15, 2020|newspaper=Memphis Commercial Appeal|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/high-school/2020/07/15/high-school-basketball-mike-miller-coach-sons-mason-and-mavrick-houston/5446661002/|access-date=August 22, 2020}} ==Personal life== Miller and his wife, Jen, have three children: sons Mason and Mavrick, and a daughter Jaelyn.[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/mike_miller/bio.html NBA.com : Mike Miller Bio Page] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080104131636/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/mike_miller/bio.html |date=January 4, 2008 }} His daughter was born during the Heat's appearance in the [[2011 NBA Playoffs#Conference Finals: (1) Chicago Bulls vs. (2) Miami Heat|2011 Eastern Conference Finals]] with a serious health issue stemming from pregnancy complications; he spent the first several days of his daughter's life shuttling between practices, games, and the hospital.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/truehoop/miamiheat/news/story?id=6588917 |title=Heat's Mike Miller thinking of daughter |first=Michael |last=Wallace |work=Miami Heat Index |publisher=[[ESPN.com]] |date=May 25, 2011 |access-date=October 19, 2020}} He once owned a [[Crab-eating macaque|Java macaque]] named Sonny. He often tells the story in which his monkey escaped from his room: "You would always put him in his room, and then we'd lock the door, and then we'd put the dogs out, and then we'd lock the front door. Well, he found out how to unlock doors, unlocked his door, went downstairs, let the dogs in the house and opened the front door. About an hour later we got a call from our neighbors, saying, 'Your monkey is riding your dogs around the neighborhood.' ... I said, 'C'mon y'all, y'all got to get in the house."{{cite news|last=Steinberg |first=Dan |url=http://voices.washingtonpost.com/dcsportsbog/2009/07/on_mike_millers_pet_monkey_and.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121014235752/http://voices.washingtonpost.com/dcsportsbog/2009/07/on_mike_millers_pet_monkey_and.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=October 14, 2012|title=On Mike Miller's Pet Monkey, and His Jump Shot |newspaper=The Washington Post |date=July 16, 2009 |access-date=October 19, 2020}}{{cite web|author=Christie Huckeba |url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/miller_monkey_010910.html |title=Mike Miller Monkeys Around |work=NBA.com|access-date=December 18, 2010}} ===Let It Fly Energy=== In 2012, Miller founded the Let It Fly Energy line of energy drinks and energy shots. In a 2012 ''Forbes'' article, he said he started the company because he wanted a healthy alternative energy drink for athletes.[https://www.forbes.com/sites/lancemadden/2012/11/05/miami-heats-mike-miller-launches-let-it-fly-energy-drink-publicly/ Miami Heat's Mike Miller Launches 'Let it Fly' Energy Drink Publicly]
